items.title: [20.0][MIG] sale_stock_picking_invoice_link: Migration to 20.0
items.body:
Migration of `sale_stock_picking_invoice_link` to 20.0.

### What the jump needed

- **`uom.uom.rounding` is gone** ([9a4ad7cc18d3](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/commit/9a4ad7cc18d3), `[REF] *: remove 'uom.uom.rounding' field`). The check on the quantity left to invoice now calls `uom.is_zero()`, which rounds with the same `Product Unit` decimal precision the removed field exposed.
- **The return wizard `stock.return.picking` is gone** ([36b4a0f5fb2b](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/commit/36b4a0f5fb2b), `[REM] stock: remove return wizard`). Two tests used it to build the return; they now call `stock.picking._create_return()`. The return move inherits `to_refund` from the original move and its demand starts at 0, so the test sets `product_uom_qty`.
- **ruff**: the 20.0 branch pins 0.16.8 and 19.0 pins 0.13.0, so `PERF102` now fails on `setUpClass`, in code this migration does not otherwise touch. `company_data` is a plain dict and the key was unused.

### It also carries the fix of #2535

#2535 (`[FIX] ... link deliveries to the invoice, not the refund`) is still open against 19.0. Without it the bug travels to 20.0: `stock_account` sets `to_refund` by `default=True` on every move, so an outgoing move of an order that has a credit note gets linked to the credit note and the invoice ends up with no pickings. If you want this PR to be the migration only, I can drop that commit and port the fix separately once #2535 is merged.

One note on it: **the `sudo()` it adds on the write is not needed in 20.0**. In 20.0 `stock_account` runs `_action_done` as superuser (`self = self.sudo()`, `stock_account/models/stock_move.py:249`), which 19.0 does not do (`:177`), so the write already runs with `sudo()` when a delivery is validated. It is kept to stay identical to the 19.0 fix. On 20.0 its test asserts the symptom instead: the invoice shows its delivery and the credit note does not.

### Migration script

`migrations/20.0.1.0.0/post-migration.py` re-links the deliveries that the old behaviour wrote against the credit note: the code fix only covers what is written from now on, so the rows already in `stock_move_invoice_line_rel` stay wrong without it. Then it recomputes `account.move.picking_ids` for every invoice and credit note it touched, because that field is stored and it is what the *Delivery* and *Invoices* buttons show. Plain parametrized SQL plus that recompute, no extra dependency, and it does nothing on a database that has no such rows.

It leaves alone the links that `stock_picking_invoice_link` copies on purpose when a delivered invoice is reversed without a return: there the move stays linked to the reversed invoice too, while the bug replaced the links.

Tested on a 20.0 database with two orders (`invoice_policy = order`): A, the bug state (posted invoice, credit note, validated delivery linked only to the credit note); B, a delivered invoice reversed without a return.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| A, invoice `picking_ids` | none | the delivery |
| A, credit note `picking_ids` | the delivery | none |
| B, invoice and credit note `picking_ids` | the delivery | the delivery (unchanged) |

Log: `1 wrong links removed from credit notes, 1 links written to the invoice, 0 moves left with no invoice line of their own, 2 invoices and credit notes recomputed`. A second run finds nothing.

### Depends on

#2493 (`stock_picking_invoice_link`), already merged in 20.0.

### Tests

`0 failed, 0 error(s) of 10 tests` on a 20.0 database with #2493 installed.

items.title: [16.0][ADD] stock_picking_bill_matching
items.body:
This module bridges Accounting and Warehouse by letting a vendor bill be
matched against the incoming receipts (and their `stock.move` lines) it
corresponds to — whether or not a purchase order exists.

It brings the *Bill Matching* paradigm of Odoo 18.0 back to Odoo 16, but
elevates it: the matching happens on `stock.move` lines instead of
`purchase.order.line`, so the bill is reconciled with what was actually
received, not with what was ordered. This is what makes it usable with any
document that reaches accounting before/independently of the purchase flow
(an imported electronic invoice, a supplier portal document, an EDI…).

## Use cases

**1. The bill arrives after the goods** (the most common case, and the usual
one with an imported electronic invoice — in Brazil it is the *NFe*, the
electronic invoice validated by the tax authority, whose XML carries the
invoice lines in a standardized form; elsewhere a supplier portal, an EDI, a
PDF extraction…). The receipt is validated: matching *links* the bill lines to
the receipt lines. Nothing is moved, nothing is restocked.

**2. The bill arrives while the goods are on their way.** The receipt is
draft/confirmed/assigned: matching additionally *drives the reception* — the
matched quantity is set as done and the receipt is validated, a backorder being
created for the excess quantity. This is the "Smart Auto-Reception" behaviour.

**3. No purchase order and no receipt at all** (small shop, or an imported
invoice for goods never encoded): the matching screen's **Create / Add to
Picking** turns the unmatched bill lines into a receipt, or the receipt is
created automatically when the bill is posted (company setting).

**4. The document carries a line reference.** Electronic invoices commonly
identify the buyer's order line they correspond to — in Brazil the NFe carries
`xPed` (the purchase order number) and `nItemPed` (the line number within that
order); an EDI or a supplier portal has its own variant. When both sides carry
the same reference, the pairing is arithmetic rather than a decision, and it can
be done automatically.

A single bill may mix all four: some lines already received, some pending, some
without counterpart. Each line is handled by whichever applies.

## Main features

* **Unified matching screen** (a SQL view): unmatched vendor bill lines and
  receipt lines side by side, grouped by product, and ordered so that a bill
  line is immediately followed by the receipt line(s) carrying the same
  pairing reference (the ones that could not be paired come last).
* **Ready-to-play demo data**: installing the module with demo data builds a
  complete scenario (a received shipment and a pending one of the same order
  line, the bill matching them, and a bill with nothing to match against), so
  the features can be tried without preparing anything — see *Trying it out*
  below.
* **Many-to-many linking** on top of `stock_picking_invoice_link`: partial
  billing, consolidated billing, one order line received over several
  shipments, several invoice lines covering one receipt.
* **Already received goods**: a validated receipt is only *linked* (nothing is
  re-validated), which is the everyday case — and the case that a
  link-only implementation typically misses.
* **Smart Auto-Reception**: matching a pending receipt sets the matched
  quantity as done, validates the receipt and creates a backorder for the
  excess, using native Odoo logic.
* **Automatic matching of referenced lines** (company setting): the bill lines
  whose reference a receipt line shares are matched automatically — from the
  **Match Pickings** button, and/or when the bill is posted. Only unambiguous
  cases are consumed, and every automatic action is traced in the bill chatter.
* **Smart button counters** on the bill: how many lines still have to be
  matched (**Match Pickings**) and how many receipt lines are already linked
  (**Matched Items**, hidden while empty).
* **Small shop replenishment**: generate the incoming receipt straight from the
  bill — one click on the matching screen, or automatically at posting. The
  generated receipt is traceable (origin `<bill> (bill matching)`, chatter
  message with a link back to the bill), and so is the fed receipt.
* **Cosmetic/service lines are ignored**: sections, notes, tax, payment-term
  and rounding lines, lines without a product and service lines neither appear
  in the matching screen nor in the counters, and they never keep a bill
  unmatched (a bill of only services and notes is simply matched).
* **Force Matched / Reset Force** for the accepted discrepancies (a backorder
  that will never arrive, a vendor over-billing…), and **Unmatch Selected** to
  undo a wrong match.
* **Warehouse users, not only accountants**, can read the matching screen.
* **`stock_picking_invoicing` compatibility**: matching/unmatching keeps the
  `invoiced` / `2binvoiced` state of the moves and pickings up to date.

## How the matching decides

On top of the product, the pairing uses a `matching_reference` char field
present on both `stock.move` and `account.move.line` (shown as **Match Ref.**):

* the same non-empty value on both sides means "same commercial line"
  (typically a purchase order line, e.g. `P00129-2` for the 2nd line of
  `P00129`; in Brazil the NFe `xPed`/`nItemPed` pair is exactly that);
* it identifies the **order line, not the shipment**: an order line received in
  several deliveries legitimately carries the same reference on each of them —
  the matching consumes them in order, already received shipments first, before
  validating a pending one. Making the reference unique per receipt would be
  wrong: an invoice does not say which shipment it corresponds to, and
  reconciling one invoice against several deliveries would become impossible;
* an **empty** reference means *unspecified* and acts as a **wildcard** (any
  line of the same product), so product-only matching keeps working when only
  one side carries a reference; exact references are consumed first;
* quantities are matched with a small epsilon (`MATCHING_PRECISION` in the ORM,
  `MATCHING_EPSILON_SQL` in the view), never rounded: a one-unit shortage is a
  shortage, not a match.

The bill-side *Unmatched Qty* never goes below zero (a line fully covered by a
larger receipt line reads 0, since the link records the pairing and not a
quantity per link); on the receipt side the value keeps its sign, where a
negative figure means the vendor billed more than what was received.

## Trying it out

Installing the module **with demo data** (a new demo database, the standard
flow) builds a small scenario — supplier *DEMO Supplier (bill matching)*, two
receipts and two bills — so every feature can be played immediately:

| Record | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| receipt *DEMO-PO-1 (1st shipment)* | **Done**: 4 Acoustic Bloc Screens, already received |
| receipt *DEMO-PO-1 (2nd shipment)* | **Ready**: 8 Acoustic Bloc Screens of the same order line, still on its way |
| draft bill *DEMO - order DEMO-PO-1 (received + on its way)* | 4 + 6 units both carrying the reference `DEMO-PO-1`, plus a section line and a service line |
| draft bill *DEMO - nothing received yet (small shop flow)* | 12 Office Chairs, no receipt and no purchase order |

Both receipts and the two storable bill lines carry the matching reference
`DEMO-PO-1` (the *Match Ref.* column): the demo sets the `matching_reference`
field explicitly, exactly what a localization computes for you (in Brazil, from
the NFe `xPed`/`nItemPed`), so the pairing works out of the box in a plain demo
database.

1. **Bill after the goods, one order line received in two shipments**: open the
   first bill → *Match Pickings* → *Match Selected* on the two storable lines.
   The 4 units already received are only **linked** (nothing is re-validated,
   nothing is restocked), the 6 units still on their way are **received** by the
   matching and the 2 excess units of that receipt become a **backorder**, and
   the section and service lines are ignored (they are never counted as
   unmatched). The *Match Pickings* counter then reads 0 and *Matched Items* 2.
2. **Automatic matching**: enable *Auto-Match Referenced Lines* in the settings,
   reopen the bill and click *Match Pickings* once — the references pair
   everything with no selection. Add *Auto-Match when Posting the Bill* to have
   it happen by itself at posting.
3. **Small shop flow**: open the second bill (nothing to match against, no
   receipt, no purchase order) → *Create / Add to Picking* builds the receipt;
   or enable *Auto-Create the Receipt when Posting the Bill* together with
   *Auto-Validate Generated Pickings* and simply post the bill: the receipt is
   created, linked, validated, and both documents are traced in each other's
   chatter.

## Company settings

Under **Inventory → Configuration → Settings → Bill Matching** (per company,
all off by default):

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Auto-Create Picking on Match** | Clicking **Match Pickings** on a bill with no open receipt (and no open purchase order) creates the missing receipt instead of opening the screen. |
| **Auto-Validate Generated Pickings** | The receipts the matching has to validate are validated straight away (small shop: the stock enters immediately). |
| **Auto-Match Referenced Lines** | Match the bill lines whose reference a receipt line shares. |
| **Auto-Match when Posting the Bill** | Also do it when the bill is posted (requires the setting above). |
| **Auto-Create the Receipt when Posting the Bill** | Small shop flow: a posted bill whose lines have nothing to match against (no purchase order, no receipt candidate) generates its own receipt, linked to the bill. |

Recommended presets:

* *Warehouse-driven* (purchase orders and receipts exist, an operator
  reconciles): everything off, optionally **Auto-Validate Generated
  Pickings**;
* *Imported documents with references* (the Brazilian NFe and its
  `xPed`/`nItemPed`, or any importer synthesizing references):
  **Auto-Match Referenced Lines** + **Auto-Match when Posting the Bill**;
* *Small shop, imported documents, nothing encoded in Odoo*: the two above plus
  **Auto-Create the Receipt when Posting the Bill** and **Auto-Validate
  Generated Pickings**.

## Posting is never blocked by the warehouse

The automation triggered at posting (automatic matching and automatic receipt
creation) runs inside a savepoint and under `try/except (UserError,
ValidationError)`. A warehouse problem posts the bill anyway and explains in
the bill chatter what failed and to match the receipts by hand; the half-done
warehouse writes are rolled back, so no orphan receipt is left behind.

## Integration contract (for localizations and importers)

The module has **no hard dependency** on any localization or importer, and
neither do they on it: everything below is duck-typed, and the feature simply
stays inactive when the absent piece is not installed.

* **`matching_reference`** (`Char`, on `stock.move` and `account.move.line`) —
  the pairing key described above; can be written directly by an importer.
* **`_get_bill_matching_reference_sql(alias)`** (on `stock.move` and/or
  `account.move.line`) — returns the SQL expression computing the reference for
  the given table alias, since the matching screen is a SQL view. The
  derivation takes precedence; the stored `matching_reference` is the fallback,
  so an importer writing the field directly gets pairing with or without a
  localization. Both sides must be normalized identically (`P00015-1` and
  `P00015-0001` must end up as the same string).
* **`_get_matching_pairs(aml_lines, sm_lines)`** — the pairing core:
  receives the selected bill lines and receipt lines and returns the
  `(bill line, receipt lines to consume)` pairs. Override it to change the
  policy itself; the caller then distributes quantities, links the lines,
  validates the pending receipts and computes the backorders.

A real-world consumer of this contract is the Brazilian localization: the NFe
import wizard of `l10n-brazil` (OCA/l10n-brazil#5346) lets the operator pick the
originating purchase order line / incoming receipt while importing the XML, and
writes the canonical reference (`<purchase order name>-<line number>`) on both
sides — which this module then pairs and matches automatically, without either
repository depending on the other.

## Compatibility

* Depends on `purchase_stock`, `stock_picking_invoice_link`,
  `purchase_stock_picking_invoice_link`; nothing else.
* Ships its own demo scenario (see *Trying it out*) — the receipts, the bills
  and the pairing references are built at installation, in a database created
  with demo data.
* Tested on 16.0 (`stock_picking_bill_matching/tests/test_stock_bill_matching.py`,
  35 test methods: done and pending receipts, backorders, partial/consolidated
  invoicing, reference pairing and non-cross matching, split deliveries,
  automatic matching on button/posting, counters, cosmetic and service line
  filtering, screen ordering, all-matched feedback, receipt traceability
  (generated and fed), stock-user access, consumables policy, and the
  automatic receipt creation at posting including its failure rollback).

## For reviewers

The interesting parts to look at, in order of "worth a debate":

1. the reference contract and the wildcard rule (the split-delivery semantics
   above) — this is what localizations hook into;
2. the two directions of matching (linking a done receipt vs driving a pending
   one) and the `unmatched_qty` sign convention;
3. the automatic matching policy: only non-empty references shared with a
   receipt line of the same vendor and product are consumed by the automatic
   path — a wrong automatic match is worse than a click;
4. the posting automation: the conservative rule for the automatic receipt
   creation (nothing is created when a purchase order or a receipt candidate
   exists) and the savepoint ensuring accounting is never blocked;
5. the smart button counters and the single line-filtering helper
   (`_get_bill_product_lines`) they share with the engine, so they can never
   disagree.

## Recent changes in this draft

Since the first version of this PR, the module went through a review and
hardening pass:

* **fixed a blocker**: a bill could not be matched against an *already
  validated* receipt (the engine only considered draft/confirmed/assigned
  moves, and the quantity to link was 0 once the receipt was done). The
  quantity left to *receive* (pending receipts, which matching drives) is now
  distinguished from the capacity left to *bill* (done receipts, only linked) —
  that is the module's main use case, since the bill usually arrives after the
  goods;
* fixed the UoM rounding used by `is_picking_matched` (the precision *digits*
  were used as the rounding), the negative bill-side `unmatched_qty`, the
  vacuous "matched" state of a purchase order without receipt, and the overwrite
  of the quantity to validate when several bill lines consumed one receipt line;
* added the automatic matching of referenced lines (button and posting), the
  smart button counters, the generated/fed receipt traceability (origin +
  chatter with a link back to the bill) and the corresponding settings;
* added the automatic receipt creation when posting, with the savepoint
  guarantee that the posting is never blocked (and never left half-done);
* the matching screen is now ordered by pairing reference inside each product
  group, and readable by warehouse users;
* the demo data was rewritten: it now builds a complete scenario (a received
  shipment, a pending one of the same order line, the bills matching them, the
  pairing references, a service/section bill, a bill with nothing to match)
  where the previous version only created two draft transfers and no bill at
  all, leaving nothing to match with out of the box;
* documentation rewritten around the use cases (`readme/DESCRIPTION.md`,
  `CONFIGURE.md`, `USAGE.md`), and the test suite grown from 9 to 35 methods.



# Stock Picking Bill Matching

This module bridges the gap between Accounting and Warehouse operations in Odoo by allowing users to match Vendor Bills directly against Incoming Stock Pickings, bypassing the need for a Purchase Order.

It brings a paradigm native to Odoo 18.0 (Bill Matching) into Odoo 16 but elevates it by matching against `stock.move` lines instead of `purchase.order.line`.

## Key Features
* **Unified Matching Interface:** A single screen (SQL View) showing unmatched Vendor Bill lines and Incoming Receipt lines side-by-side.
* **Many-to-Many Linking:** Leverages the `stock_picking_invoice_link` OCA module to allow complex many-to-many relationships (e.g., partial billing, consolidated billing).
* **Smart Auto-Reception:** Matching bill lines with pending receipts automatically validates the receipt and handles backorders safely using native Odoo logic.
* **Small Shop Replenishment:** Easily generate brand-new Incoming Receipts straight from a drafted Vendor Bill with a single click.
* **Extensibility:** Built with an extensible matching hook (`_get_matching_pairs`) to allow localization modules (like the Brazilian NFe `xPed`/`nItemPed`) to override the default product-based matching behavior.
* **Compatibility:** If the `stock_picking_invoicing` module is installed, matching or unmatching lines automatically updates the invoice state (`invoiced` / `2binvoiced`) on stock moves and pickings.




# Usage

## Testing with Demo Data
This module includes demo data to easily test the matching workflows.
1. Ensure your database is loaded with demo data.
2. Go to **Accounting -> Vendors -> Bills**.
3. Look for the Draft bill assigned to **Deco Addict** (Reference: `Demo Bill`).
4. Go to **Inventory -> Receipts**. You will see two incoming receipts for Deco Addict
   generated by the demo data.

## 1. Matching Existing Pickings and Bills
If you receive an electronic invoice and the warehouse has already processed the receipt:
1. Open the Vendor Bill.
2. Click the **Match Pickings** smart button at the top right.
3. You will be taken to the matching view.
4. Select the Vendor Bill line(s) and the corresponding Receipt line(s).
   * *Note: They are grouped by product, with Vendor Bills appearing above Receipts.*
5. Click **Match Selected**.
   * The lines will vanish from the Unmatched view.
   * If the Receipt had a higher quantity than the Bill, Odoo will automatically create a Backorder for the remaining quantity.
   * If the Bill had a higher quantity, the remaining billed quantity will stay in the view awaiting a future receipt, or you can create a new picking for it using the **Create / Add to Picking** button.

## 2. "Small Shop" Replenishment (Auto-Create Pickings)
If you do not use Purchase Orders and simply import electronic Vendor Bills, you can generate your warehouse receipts in one click:
1. Open the Draft Vendor Bill.
2. Click the **Match Pickings** smart button.
3. In the matching view, select all vendor bill lines and click **Create / Add to Picking** in the header.
4. A wizard will appear. Leave the "Existing Picking" field blank.
5. Check the **Auto-Validate Receipt** checkbox if you want the stock to immediately enter your warehouse.
6. Click **Confirm**. The system will generate a `WH/IN` picking, populate it with all unmatched lines from the bill, and link them permanently.

*Tip: If the company setting **Auto-Create Picking on Match** is enabled, clicking **Match Pickings** on a bill with no open receipts will skip the matching view and generate the picking automatically.*

## 3. Undo / Unmatching
If you made a mistake:
1. Go to the Vendor Bill and click the **Matched Items** smart button.
2. Select the mistakenly matched lines.
3. Click **Unmatch Selected**. The Many-to-Many links will be severed, and the quantities will return to the **Match Pickings** view.

items.title: [16.0] [FIX] stock_picking_invoice_link: remove duplicated element in stock.move form view
[19.0][FIX] stock_picking_invoice_link: restrict the invoice link to invoicing users
items.body:
## Problem

A user with **Inventory / User** access and no accounting access cannot open an
internal transfer once this module is installed. The form fails with:

```
AccessError: Failed to read field stock.picking.invoice_ids
You are not allowed to access 'Journal Entry' (account.move) records.
```

The picking form injects `invoice_ids` (m2m to `account.move`) and the *Invoice*
stat button with no `groups`. Reading a many2many triggers a search on the
comodel, and warehouse profiles have no read access on `account.move`, so an
accessory piece of information ends up blocking the core operation of the role.

The same happens on the **stock.move** form with `invoice_line_ids`
(`account.move.line`).

## Why `groups` on the field was not enough

`invoice_line_ids` already carried `groups="account.group_account_invoice"`, but
the surrounding `<group>` has an `invisible="invoice_line_ids == []"` modifier.
View postprocessing adds the field back as an invisible node so the modifier can
be evaluated:

```xml
<field name="invoice_line_ids" invisible="True" readonly="True"
       data-used-by="invisible='invoice_line_ids == []' (group,invoice_line)"/>
```

so the field is read anyway and the form still breaks. The fix puts `groups` on
the node that carries the modifier, which removes both the modifier and the
field.

## Change

`views/stock_view.xml` only:

- picking form: `groups="account.group_account_invoice"` on the `invoice_ids`
  field and on the stat button (the button holds the
  `invisible="invoice_count == 0"` modifier, so it goes away with it);
- move form: `groups` moved from the `invoice_line_ids` field to the enclosing
  `<group name="invoice_line">`.

Nothing changes for users who can already see invoices.

## Test plan

On a 19.0 database with this module installed, a user whose only groups are
`base.group_user` + `stock.group_stock_user`:

- **before**: `picking.read(<fields exposed by stock.view_picking_form>)` raises
  `AccessError` on `account.move`; the same on `stock.view_move_form` raises on
  `account.move.line`;
- **after**: `invoice_ids` / `invoice_count` / `invoice_line_ids` are no longer
  present in the arch returned by `get_view()` for that user, and reading every
  field the forms expose succeeds;
- a user with `account.group_account_invoice` still gets the stat button, the
  invoice lines group and `invoice_count`, and reaches the invoice from the
  picking.

The list views (`stock.vpicktree`, `stock.view_move_tree`) never exposed these
fields, and were verified not to raise for the restricted user.

The same asymmetry is present on 18.0; a backport can follow once this is
reviewed.

## Current Scenario

The stock_picking_invoice_link module, which adds the relationship between the invoice and stock picking, depends on the sale_stock module, but the purchase_stock_picking_invoice_link module depends on stock_picking_invoice_link, making it mandatory to install both the purchase and sale modules, thus losing modularity.

## Proposed Solution

The sale dependency on stock_picking_invoice_link was removed, and a new sale_stock_picking_invoice_link module was created. In this way, the stock_picking_invoice_link module is a base module for the sale_stock_picking_invoice_link and purchase_stock_picking_invoice_link modules, preserving modularity.

This PR introduces a restriction to prevent the cancellation of stock moves that are already linked to invoices or vendor bills. Only users who are members of the "Allow to cancel stock moves linked to invoices/bills" group will be authorized to perform this action.

## Why Restrict Cancelling Stock Moves Linked to Invoices/Bills

- **Data Integrity**: Prevents inconsistencies between inventory and accounting.
- **Controlled Access**: Cancellation is still allowed, but only for users in the designated security group.
- **Legal and Financial Compliance**: Avoids issues with invoiced or billed records.
- **Auditability**: Maintains a clear and traceable record of exceptional actions.
- **Best Practice**: Encourages using proper workflows like credit notes or returns.
